title: The 30 ACE source views have no owner in the Ownership Map
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
section: Fields (the 30 recovery.v_ace_* entities and their 304 fields)
description: The Fields tab classifies 304 fields of the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views. The Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables lists 93 Workbench tables and no view, so the Owner column appended in v5 has no map row for those 304 fields and the ownership of the view contract has to be read from the architecture instead.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 707 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views), line 850 (SQL view: only rwb-source-data, read-only login, 30 views), lines 2147 and 2884 (schema recovery holds the 30 views; P1 owns the ACE view contract and the extension tables); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables, 93 rows, none of them a v_ace_* view; DP-05; ADR-010.
proposed: P1 rwb-source-data owns the 30 views under the ACE view contract. The Owner column reads P1 rwb-source-data (recovery view) on all 304 view fields, and no other service login holds a grant on a view.

title: payment_match_rule is in the inventory but not in the Ownership Map, and D-RCV-36 retires it as a table
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
description: The Fields tab classifies the 13 fields of payment_match_rule. The Ownership Map has no row for the table, and PRD P8 records it retired by D-RCV-36: the values become versioned parameter and reference rows and the logic becomes the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package, so the entity has an owner and a disposition that the inventory does not state.
evidence: PRD P8 rwb-payment v1 lines 123, 169 and 250 (payment_match_rule retired by D-RCV-36; versioned parameter and reference rows in rwb-case and the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package in rwb-decision); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 1084 (PAYMENT_MATCH replaces payment_match_rule, T10); Physical Schema v6.sql rows DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables, no row payment_match_rule.
proposed: The 13 rows are kept with their field IDs and marked retired as a table. The Owner column reads P3 rwb-case (retired table) because the values live as versioned reference rows there, and the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package is P7 rwb-decision.

title: lake_copy_watermark is still an entity of the inventory although the data lake is removed
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
description: Six fields of lake_copy_watermark are classified as Workbench data. The target architecture has no data lake and no Power BI connection, so the table has nothing to watermark and the inventory still presents it as live data with an on-screen rule and a retention rule.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 67 and line 707 (Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19 and INT-20 removed), line 2988 (JOB-13: the decision log copy is replaced by continuous Kafka ingest); ADR-018; DP-17; Template and Rules R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired).
proposed: The six rows are kept with their field IDs and marked retired with the data lake; the Owner column reads P1 rwb-source-data (retired table) and no copy is built.

title: OCR text is classified Not personal while the same content at field level is Restricted
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
description: document_text.text_content, the OCR text of a page of a customer document, is classified Not personal and Internal with the note masked by role on read, while document_field.field_value, the same content read as a field, is a Direct identifier at Restricted. One of the two rows must be wrong, and the field-level rule for events, workflow inputs and logs cannot be read from the category alone.
evidence: v4 Fields DF-DOC-089 (Not personal; Internal; No; Shown by permission; Meaning: OCR text of the page; masked by role on read) against DF-DOC-015 (Direct identifier; Restricted; Yes; Masked unless the role may see it); v4 Handling row 5 (Restricted fields encrypted at rest) and row 21 (contact values masked for display); Key row 5 (Direct identifier identifies a person on its own, free text about them).
proposed: The classification is left for the data steward. In this version the row carries the rule never in an event, a workflow input or a log, and the page id only in a log, which is what a Restricted field gets.

title: One recovery identity reads the ACE views; the target has one login and one schema per service
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
section: Handling (Restricted, Every ACE read; Restricted, In logs)
description: The Handling tab gives the recovery identity SELECT on recovery.v_ace_* and assumes that any service may read a view. Under D-RCV-60 there are 19 schemas and 19 logins, only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views, and no other login has a grant on them or on public, so the rule and the read-audit path change.
evidence: v4 Handling rows 7 and 22 (the recovery identity holds SELECT only on recovery.v_ace_*; every read of a v_ace_* personal field is logged through PII Kafka); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 509, 707, 909, 2051, 2126, 2143, 2147, 2533, 3016, 3038 (one login and one schema per service; only rwb-source-data reads the views); ADR-010; ADR-014; DP-01; DP-02; DP-05.
proposed: Only the rwb_source_data login holds SELECT on the 30 views; every other service reads the same data through the P1 REST contract or a Temporal activity, and the read audit is written through the ACE Common PII logging path.

title: The PII log path is named PII Kafka with no owner and no separation from the business topics
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
description: The inventory sends every read of a personal field to PII Kafka and records the read audit in the access log, without saying that this is the ACE Common path to the SOC or that the Recovery business topics are a different set of topics. A reader can conclude that a personal field may travel on rwb.<service>.events.v1.
evidence: v4 Handling row 7 (logged through PII Kafka) and row 22 (a read is audited); v4 Key row 16 (written to the access log through PII Kafka); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 511 (ACE Common gives audit and PII logging, PII Kafka to SOC), line 1503 (Recovery business-event topics separate from ACE's PII logging topics), lines 2179 to 2183 (Kafka PII path to SOC) and line 2537 (ACE PII logging to SOC).
proposed: The rule names the ACE Common PII logging path to the SOC (INT-34) and states that the business topics are separate and carry no personal data.

title: The masking rule has no owner on the page that lists who sees what
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
section: Who sees what (note row 2 and the 14 role rows)
description: The sheet is proposed until Compliance issues the masking rules under DL26 and names no owner for the rule. Under D-RCV-60 the masking policy is P4 rwb-access data, enforced in each service, so the page needs the owner and where the rule is applied.
evidence: v4 Who sees what A2 (proposed until Compliance issues the masking rules, DL26); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 1020 (P4 writes the masking policy in rwb_access), line 2882 (P4 owns masking policy), line 2562 (masking rules (P4) enforced in each service), line 776 (ACE data masked by policy at the gateway); RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
proposed: An Enforced by column names P4 rwb-access for the policy, the owning service that applies it, P10 rwb-agent for a prompt and the P1 login for an ACE value; DL26 still owns the rule content.

title: The inventory has no rule for events, workflow inputs or logs
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
description: The inventory classifies storage, screens, prompts, test data, export and the debt sale tape, but it has no rule for a Kafka event, a Temporal workflow input or history, or an application log. Those are the three channels the realignment must close, so every field carries no statement about what may leave the service.
evidence: v4 Handling B5 to B22 (Where values: Stored, On screen, In logs, In agent prompts, In test data, Export, Debt sale tape, Retention, Data subject request, In ACE, Contact values, Every ACE read) has no row for an event or a workflow; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 833 (Never: personal data in events, I/O or PII in workflow code or payloads), line 1618 (Payload: IDs and business facts, no PII), line 3064 and Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 1885 (payload codec, search attributes); Template and Rules R7.2 s17.
proposed: Three appended columns on Fields and Identifiers, six new Handling rows and a new PII controls sheet give the rule per field and per channel, with the owner of each control.

title: The interaction ledger is defined by the case module but the Ownership Map gives it to P1
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Classification and Personal Data Inventory v4.xlsx
description: The interaction entity carries 29 classified fields and the case timeline reads it. The Ownership Map gives the ledger to P1 rwb-source-data under the R-PREC default ruling and keeps the timeline API with P3 rwb-case, so the Owner column shows P1 on 29 fields that a reader of this inventory would expect on the case service.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings row interaction (ledger and intake rule stay with P1; the case timeline and interaction API stay with P3, ASM-A6-tables-1); Ownership Map sheet Tables row interaction (P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2884 (P1 owns the ACE view contract and the extension tables) and Template and Rules R3 default ruling list (interaction ledger, P1); DP-18.
proposed: The Owner column follows the map: P1 rwb-source-data on the 29 interaction fields, and P3 rwb-case reads the ledger through the P1 contract for the case timeline.
